chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام
about roofed mosques, whether standing in them is disliked. He said: “Yes, but salat (prayer) in them does not harm you.”

key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: is disliked, indicating karāhah rather than prohibition
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), the act whose validity is being affirmed
key_terms.ٱلْقِيَامُ: standing, referring here to standing in prayer
key_terms.ٱلْمَسَاجِدِ: mosques, the places of worship being discussed
key_terms.ٱلْمُظَلَّلَةِ: covered or roofed, describing the type of mosques mentioned

ai.seo_question: Is praying in covered or roofed mosques disliked in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on performing salat (prayer) in roofed or covered mosques. It indicates that standing in such mosques is regarded as disliked, yet praying in them remains valid and does not cause harm.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.705 - Ubaidullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about covered (roofed) mosques, whether standing (prayer) in them is disliked.
Imam (as) said: "Yes, but praying in them does not harm you."
